base_member_text: [L1369-L1385] (MED/ignored-argument-access) Alltoallw dereferences the send-datatype array even for an in-place intracommunicator call where send arguments are ignored.
audit_member_text: [L1373-L1377,L1385] (MED/ignored-argument-access) Alltoallw dereferences the send-datatype array before MPI can ignore it for an in-place operation, so an otherwise valid ignored null argument can fail in the wrapper.

adversarial.rationale: The bundled mpi.h advertises MPI 2.2, whose [Alltoallw contract](https://www.mpi-forum.org/docs/mpi-2.2/mpi22-report/node101.htm) permits in-place intracommunicator calls with ignored sendtypes. The wrapper unconditionally reads v4 for Get_size entries before the C call, and neither the class hierarchy nor a preprocessor branch adds an MPI_IN_PLACE guard.

base_member_text: [L1369-L1385,L1516,L1545-L1548] (HIGH/intercommunicator-size) Alltoallw sizes and copies datatype arrays using local Get_size although an intercommunicator requires remote-group lengths, causing out-of-bounds accesses when group sizes differ.
audit_member_text: [L1369-L1385,L1545-L1549] (HIGH/collective-buffer-sizing) Alltoallw sizes and copies datatype arrays using local Get_size even on an Intercomm, although unequal remote-group sizes require different array lengths.

adversarial.rationale: Intercomm inherits Comm::Alltoallw without overriding Get_size, which calls MPI_Comm_size at L1285-L1289; Get_remote_size is a distinct method. Unequal groups therefore produce an overread of caller arrays on the larger local group and undersized C datatype temporaries on the smaller group; the [MPI 2.2 intercommunicator contract](https://www.mpi-forum.org/docs/mpi-2.2/mpi22-report/node101.htm) requires communication with the remote group.
adversarial.verified_by: llm:codex gpt-6-astra skeptic + caller verbatim neutralizer re-check

audit_member_text: [L236-L244,L790-L803,L985-L1006,L1371-L1387,L1692-L1702] (MED/exception-safety) Raw temporary arrays are freed and modified request handles copied back only after error-handler calls, so a thrown MPI exception leaks allocations and can leave caller request handles stale.

adversarial.rationale: All cited temporaries are raw allocations, with copy-back and deletion after the MPIX_CALL macros, and there are no catch/RAII cleanup blocks. The shipped cxx.lib Call_errhandler implementation does throw for ERRORS_THROW_EXCEPTIONS, so an error can skip request copy-back and frees; failure of a second new also leaks the first allocation.

base_member_text: [L1568-L1579,L1659-L1670,L2329-L2340,L2444-L2455] (MED/clone-error-handling) Clone methods ignore MPI_Comm_dup status and construct objects from an uninitialized ncomm on a returned error, unlike the checked Dup methods.
audit_member_text: [L1568-L1578,L1659-L1669,L2329-L2339,L2444-L2454] (MED/error-propagation) Clone ignores MPI_Comm_dup status and constructs a communicator from potentially uninitialized ncomm instead of applying the error-handling path used by Dup.

adversarial.rationale: Both Clone preprocessor variants ignore MPI_Comm_dup status, but the C routine itself invokes its configured error handler, so Clone does not bypass every error-handling path. Retain MED only for returned-error configurations: wrapper-side dispatch, especially the C++ exception translation seen in cxx.lib, is skipped and ncomm is used without a guaranteed successful initialization; fatal C error handling prevents that continuation.

   Using the MPIR prefix preserved the MPI_ names for objects defined by
   the standard. */
#define MPIR_ERRORS_THROW_EXCEPTIONS ((MPI_Errhandler)0x54000002)
